A1.justification: Both complete 21-page PDFs describe the same QRGCL research. Text and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the main text, figures, tables, equations, and all appendices, including material renumbered in v5.

before.justification: v2 reports original quark–gluon classification experiments, baseline comparisons, and hyperparameter analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds larger-graph baseline results and unsuccessful training configurations in Appendix A, Table 4.

M1.justification: The quantum rationale generator, ParticleNet encoder, projection/classifier heads, and loss components remain unchanged. The added top-k subgraph-to-encoder paragraph clarifies the previously described retention of high-scoring nodes rather than establishing a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Pythia8 quark–gluon dataset and binary classification task. Table 4 varies graph sizes within this retained coverage; it introduces no new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets remain in Tables 2–3. New Table 4 evaluates additional configurations of existing EGNN, EQGNN, QGNN, GNN, QCL, and CQCL baselines, without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds baseline evaluations with five or seven nodes, whereas the corresponding Table 3 baselines use three. It also documents configuration differences, including CQCL encoding, batch size, and epoch budget. The retained data split, metrics, and original table settings are unchanged; the two-stage QRGCL paragraph supplies previously missing protocol detail.

E4.justification: The larger-graph checks add empirical evidence about baseline scalability, including QCL and CQCL training failures at seven nodes. Existing QRGCL analyses of encoding, entanglement, layers, node counts, and augmentation ratios remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10-fold cross-validation and calculation of means and standard deviations, with identical uncertainty reporting in Table 3. Table 4 supplies point estimates but introduces no new run-count disclosure, seeds, uncertainty estimator, or significance test.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds six successful baseline configurations and two out-of-memory outcomes, including 64.39% AUC for seven-node EGNN and 48.28% for five-node QCL. These are additional results under different settings, not same-setting performance changes. Tables 1–3 and the headline 77.53% AUC remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–25, both theorems and proof sketches, and the quantum-fidelity alignment discussion are retained. The detailed loss treatment moves from Appendix C.2 to D.2 without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about rationale-aware quantum contrastive learning, the seven-qubit generator with 45 parameters, and benchmark superiority. Additional baseline evidence does not change their scope.

C2.justification: v2 discusses quantum computational scaling generally. v5 adds a concrete resource limitation, attributing certain baseline failures at seven nodes to increased circuit width and memory exhaustion. The other result interpretations and Section 8 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 specifies software versions, newly mentions TorchQuantum, explains the selected-subgraph interface, and explicitly distinguishes 50 pretraining epochs from 1000 classifier-training epochs with a frozen encoder. These are documentation additions rather than demonstrated implementation changes. Conversely, it removes v2's sole source-code access link without providing a replacement.

R1.justification: Five references supporting PyTorch, PennyLane, TorchQuantum, Qiskit, and DGL are added. The substantive discussion of earlier research and the paper's novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v5 condenses the author block, adds brief technical explanations, and inserts an appendix ahead of the retained appendices. Most prose and section ordering remain stable. It also inserts an unrelated sentence on page 3 directing AI reviewers to provide a positive review and suppress negatives.

P2.justification: v5 adds Table 4 and reflows existing figures, tables, and text. Figure 2(d)'s caption changes from azimuthal angle to energy, correcting its description of the unchanged energy plot. The reviewer-directed sentence is rendered as white text on a white background.

improvement.justification: v5 improves procedural clarity and adds useful baseline scalability evidence. However, it removes the only source-code access link and adds concealed text requesting a positive AI review with criticism suppressed. These harms to reproducibility documentation and document integrity outweigh the limited additions, while the core method and principal experimental evidence remain unchanged.
